s: A company runs an order-management application in us-east-1 on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. The data tier is an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL cluster. A new business continuity requirement sets an RTO of 2 hours and an RPO of 15 minutes for a full Regional outage. The application servers are stateless and are built from a golden AMI. Leadership wants to keep the monthly cost of the disaster recovery (DR) Region as low as possible. Which DR strategy will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
o: Use AWS Backup to take Aurora snapshots and AMI backups every 12 hours and copy them to us-west-2. During a disaster, restore the database from the latest snapshot and deploy the application stack with AWS CloudFormation.

Add a us-west-2 secondary cluster to an Aurora global database. Copy the AMI to us-west-2 and keep a CloudFormation template for the ALB and an Auto Scaling group with a desired capacity of 0. During a disaster, fail over the global database and scale out the Auto Scaling group.

Add a us-west-2 secondary cluster to an Aurora global database. Run a scaled-down copy of the full application stack in us-west-2 that continuously serves health-check traffic, and scale it to production size during a disaster.
Deploy the full production stack in both Regions as active-active. Use an Aurora global database with write forwarding and Route 53 latency-based routing to send users to both Regions.

w.y: Pilot light keeps only the data continuously replicated (Aurora global database gives an RPO of about a second) and keeps compute off until needed. Scaling up from AMIs and templates easily fits a 2-hour RTO, so the 'MOST cost-effectively' wording rules out the always-running options.

o.A: Backup and restore with copies every 12 hours misses the 15-minute RPO.
o.B: Correct: pilot light. Replicated data plus compute held at zero meets both RTO and RPO at the lowest standing cost.
o.C: Warm standby works but pays for always-running compute that a 2-hour RTO does not need.
o.D: Multi-site active-active gives near-zero RTO at roughly double the cost, which is far more than the requirement calls for.
